name: manual_8ba8fd
claim: When dual-voice adversarial review (independent Claude subagent + Codex) converges strongly against a plan, steelman the critiques before accepting the verdict — some adversarial findings dissolve on inspection (holding an MVP to a bar it explicitly disclaims in its own stated constraints), while others survive because they're verified against actual source code, not just argued

decisions.notes: On the G7 SSE plan, Codex's critiques about v2-mesh-compatibility 'not earned' and process-local fan-out being a 'hidden commitment' both dissolved once checked against the plan's own Global Constraints section, which explicitly and prominently disclaims both. But the 2 Claude-subagent-found bugs (field-name mismatch, SSE timeout leak) survived the steelman pass because they were confirmed by reading the real source, not by argument. User explicitly requested the steelman pass mid-review after seeing the adversarial dual-voice findings, worried about pile-on bias.
